models.title: Additive Fisher approximation for nominal interest
models.summary: The owner expresses nominal interest as real interest plus expected inflation.

relationship.original_equation: Nominal interest ≈ real interest + expected inflation
relationship.translation_notes: All rates are dimensionless base-one fractions for the same period.

variables.context: Same economy and rate horizon; base-one rate with matching compounding conventions

assumptions: Real interest and expected inflation use the same horizon and compatible rate conventions.
The additive relation is a first-order or log-rate approximation; a discrete gross-rate calculation includes their interaction.
limitations: Do not confuse expected with realized inflation.
Uncertainty and risk premia can complicate the interpretation of ex ante real returns.

models.title: Nominal neutral policy rate using trend growth as a proxy
models.summary: The owner estimates the neutral nominal policy rate by adding trend growth and the inflation target.

relationship.original_equation: Neutral nominal rate ≈ trend real growth + inflation target
relationship.translation_notes: Both inputs and the result are dimensionless base-one rates over a common horizon.

variables.context: Same economy and rate horizon; base-one rate with matching compounding conventions
Same economy and rate horizon; base-one rate with matching compounding conventions
Same economy and rate horizon; base-one rate with matching compounding conventions

assumptions: Trend real GDP growth is used as a proxy for the unobserved neutral real interest rate, and trend inflation equals the inflation target.
Rates share the same annualized period and additive rate convention.
limitations: The growth proxy is a modeling assumption, not an identity; the Fed paper notes the real-rate and growth relationship may be weak or change sign.
The neutral rate is unobservable and a policy-rate comparison alone does not capture every financial condition.
